messages.content: Define: an integer m is even iff there exists k in Z with m = 2k; m is odd iff there exists k in Z with m = 2k+1. We prove for each natural number n that n(n+1) is even by case analysis on parity of n. Case 1: n is even, so n = 2k; then n(n+1) = 2k(n+1) = 2(k(n+1)), which exhibits n(n+1) as twice an integer, hence even. Case 2: n is odd, so n = 2k+1; then n+1 = 2k+2 = 2(k+1), so n+1 is even, and n(n+1) = n * 2(k+1) = 2(n(k+1)), which is twice an integer, so even. The case analysis covers all integers by the law of excluded parity (every integer is even or odd). Therefore for every natural n, n(n+1) is even.
